content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes or volatility; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3% for 30-day horizons.
- When sentiment is neutral (all 0.00), model exhibits strong upward bias; apply downward adjustment of 2–5% to forecast mean if no sentiment signal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot and continue upward; cap forecast slope after 3–5 days of high volatility.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; if 3–5 consecutive days show high volatility or outlier prices, reduce forecast slope by 10–20% to reflect reversion to mean.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in capturing true price drops; if true outcome drops below 75% of prior 18-day average, adjust forecast downward by 5–10% immediately.
- Sentiment history is ignored in model, but when sentiment is non-zero (even if 0.00), model should be calibrated to reflect market sentiment; if sentiment is 0.00, assume neutral but not flat — apply slight downward bias to avoid overconfidence.
